function: Learns the adaptive priority-weight factor C that sets the user weights of a weighted-MMSE multi-user MIMO precoder across TTIs, using soft actor-critic (p. 5).
system: Downlink multi-user MIMO: 64-antenna BS, 4-antenna VR users, up to 10 active of 30 candidates, 3.5 GHz, 10 MHz, 10 dBm, no RIS (pp. 9-10).
method: Soft actor-critic reinforcement learning (actor, twin critics, 256-unit layers), 20,000 training steps in simulation, outputs a factor for a non-learned WMMSE precoder (pp. 5-6, 10).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa UMa NLOS channels at 3.5 GHz, 30 candidate users 100-200 m from the BS moving at 3 m/s; simulated Pareto/Gaussian traffic (p. 9).
test_conditions: Trained with Kmax=10 users and dynamic activation (p. 11); tested over 5,000 TTIs, 10 repetitions, with K varied from 4 to 10 users (pp. 10-11).
baselines: Non-learned: WMMSE, fixed-C WMMSE (C=2,5,10), QoS-constrained ADMM precoder with fixed C. Learned: DDPG-based weight learning (DDPG_C) in the same WMMSE pipeline (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Frame transmission utility (video and haptic reception ratio), user satisfaction ratio, system capacity at 90% satisfied users, training convergence, CPU running time (pp. 10-13).
complexity: O(Lw(K^2NtNr^2+K^2Nt^2Nr+KNt^3+KNr^3)), network inference ignored; CPU time per iteration 0.022-0.213 s for SAC vs 0.707-10.383 s for QoS (p. 13).
q1_support: p. 9: "we adopt the representative Quasi Deterministic Radio channel Generator (QuaDRiGa) channel model", UMa NLOS at 3.5 GHz; the same setup serves training and testing (Sec. V).
q2_support: p. 11: "We trained the SAC networks with a maximum value of Kmax = 10. However, we can change the user number K during the prediction stage." Figs. 6-7 vary K from 4 to 10 with a single pre-trained network (p. 5).
q3_support: p. 11: "the proposed SAC-based scheme outperforms the WMMSE-based one-time-slot precoding optimization solution and the DDPG-based RL framework", on user satisfaction and video frame utility (Figs. 6-7). DDPG_C swaps the RL algorithm in the same WMMSE pipeline (p. 10).
q4_support: p. 13: "the complexity of the SAC-based WMMSE algorithm can be given as" O(Lw(K^2 Nt Nr^2 + K^2 Nt^2 Nr + K Nt^3 + K Nr^3)); Table II gives CPU running times (SAC 0.022 s to 0.213 s). Network inference is ignored.
q5_support: p. 9: "we adopt the representative Quasi Deterministic Radio channel Generator (QuaDRiGa) channel model", a simulator rather than a released dataset. No code or data link appears in the paper.
notes: Included, area 3. Borderline above_phy: the SAC state and reward are queue and QoE quantities (remaining data, delay, frame reception), but the learned action is one factor that sets the user weights of the WMMSE precoder (p. 5), so it shapes the precoder; the paper frames the work as MIMO precoding (title, abstract). q3 rests on DDPG_C, the same WMMSE pipeline with DDPG instead of SAC (p. 10), so the reviewer may confirm it counts as a standard learning algorithm applied to the same problem. q2 rests on varying K at prediction against Kmax=10 in training (p. 11); the paper claims adaptation to different channel models (p. 3) but shows no test on another channel model. q4 covers the WMMSE stage and Table II runtime, since the network inference cost is ignored (p. 13). The QoS-constrained ADMM precoder (Sec. IV) is a second, non-learned method of the paper.
